questions.text: Locate Flask.ensure_sync, which adapts coroutine view functions.

targets.name: Flask.ensure_sync
targets.rationale: Checks iscoroutinefunction and delegates coroutine functions to async_to_sync.

questions.text: Where is copy_current_request_context implemented?

targets.name: copy_current_request_context
targets.rationale: Copies the active request context and returns a wrapper that runs the callable inside it.

questions.text: Find the SessionInterface policy that decides whether to set a session cookie.

targets.name: SessionInterface.should_set_cookie
targets.rationale: Returns true for modified sessions or permanent sessions requiring refresh.

questions.text: Locate Flask.make_default_options_response.

targets.name: Flask.make_default_options_response
targets.rationale: Gets allowed methods from the URL adapter and populates the response Allow header.

questions.text: Which implementation stops processing before-request hooks when one returns a response?

targets.name: Flask.preprocess_request
targets.rationale: Iterates preprocessors and before-request functions, returning the first non-None value.

questions.text: Where does routing choose between an automatic OPTIONS response and invoking the endpoint view?

targets.name: Flask.dispatch_request
targets.rationale: Checks the rule and request method before selecting the endpoint and passing view arguments.

questions.text: Where does a view that returns None get rejected as an invalid response?

targets.name: Flask.make_response
targets.rationale: Raises TypeError when the unpacked return value is None.

questions.text: How are explicitly supplied template variables kept from being overwritten by context processors?

targets.name: Flask.update_template_context
targets.rationale: Copies the original context, applies processors, then restores the original values.

questions.text: Where does an invalid signed session cookie fall back to an empty session?

targets.name: SecureCookieSessionInterface.open_session
targets.rationale: Catches BadSignature from serializer loading and returns a new session_class instance.

questions.text: Which code deletes the session cookie when an emptied session was modified?

targets.name: SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session
targets.rationale: In the empty-session branch, deletes the cookie only if modified and updates Vary.

questions.text: Where is the decision made to indent JSON responses in debug mode or use compact separators?

targets.name: DefaultJSONProvider.response
targets.rationale: Selects indent=2 or compact separators using the provider compact option and app.debug.

questions.text: Which code retrieves flashed messages once per request and filters them by category?

targets.name: get_flashed_messages
targets.rationale: Caches popped session flashes on request_ctx and applies category_filter before formatting.

questions.text: Trace template rendering across modules from render_template to applying context processors.

targets.name: render_template
targets.rationale: Obtains the template and passes it to _render.

targets.name: _render
targets.rationale: Calls app.update_template_context before rendering.

targets.name: Flask.update_template_context
targets.rationale: Runs the registered processors and preserves caller-provided variables.

questions.text: Which helper and application method turn arguments to flask.make_response into a response object?

targets.name: make_response
targets.rationale: Normalizes positional arguments and delegates to current_app.make_response.

targets.name: Flask.make_response
targets.rationale: Unpacks response tuples and converts supported return types into the response class.

questions.text: Trace the public URL-building helper to the application code that expands a blueprint-relative endpoint.

targets.name: url_for
targets.rationale: Forwards the endpoint and special keyword arguments to current_app.url_for.

targets.name: Flask.url_for
targets.rationale: Expands endpoints starting with a dot using the current blueprint before adapter.build.

questions.text: Which WSGI entry code pushes a request context, and where does that push open the session?

targets.name: Flask.wsgi_app
targets.rationale: Creates and pushes the request context before dispatch.

targets.name: RequestContext.push
targets.rationale: Invokes session_interface.open_session and installs a null session if necessary.

questions.text: Trace saving the default cookie session from response processing into the session backend.

targets.name: Flask.process_response
targets.rationale: Calls the configured session interface after response hooks for non-null sessions.

targets.name: SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session
targets.rationale: Serializes the session and writes or deletes the response cookie.

questions.text: Which public jsonify function and default provider implementation produce the JSON HTTP response?

targets.name: jsonify
targets.rationale: Delegates positional and keyword arguments to current_app.json.response.

targets.name: DefaultJSONProvider.response
targets.rationale: Serializes the prepared object and constructs the application response with JSON MIME type.

questions.text: How does template streaming keep an active request context while yielding output across module boundaries?

targets.name: _stream
targets.rationale: Wraps the generated template iterator with stream_with_context when a request exists.

targets.name: stream_with_context
targets.rationale: Starts a wrapper iterator that retains the current request context while yielding source items.

questions.text: Trace request-context removal to execution of registered teardown handlers.

targets.name: RequestContext.pop
targets.rationale: On the outermost pop, calls app.do_teardown_request before resetting context tokens.

targets.name: Flask.do_teardown_request
targets.rationale: Runs teardown functions in reverse registration order and emits the teardown signal.

questions.text: Which test checks the default OPTIONS Allow header and empty response body?

targets.name: test_options_work
targets.rationale: Asserts GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and POST are allowed and the response data is empty.

questions.text: Which test verifies that an early before-request response prevents later hooks and the view from running?

targets.name: test_request_preprocessing_early_return
targets.rationale: Records events and asserts only the first two hooks ran and the early response was returned.

questions.text: Find the test showing that an explicitly supplied template variable named config takes precedence.

targets.name: test_original_win
targets.rationale: Renders config=42 and asserts the output is 42 rather than the standard config object.

questions.text: Which test checks that a session without a secret key can be read but rejects mutation?

targets.name: test_missing_session
targets.rationale: Sets secret_key=None, reads a missing item and asserts mutating operations raise RuntimeError.
